content.text:
I submitted **index 0 (Bi 0.97, Sb 0.03)** as the best composition, but every EQE I measured was tiny, so this library looks close to inactive at 2.4 eV.

| Index | Composition (Bi/Sb) | Nearby known phase | Measured EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.97 / 0.03 | Bi₂O₃ | 3.1×10⁻⁴ |
| 5 | 0.93 / 0.07 | Bi₁₂SbO₂₀ | 8.7×10⁻⁵ |
| 14 | 0.75 / 0.25 | Bi₃SbO₇ | −4.7×10⁻⁵ (effectively zero) |

**How I chose:** I only had 3 merit measurements across 30 candidates, so I used predicted band gaps to decide where to look. The Bi-rich phases are predicted to absorb 2.4 eV light:
- Bi₁₂SbO₂₀: 1.68 eV
- Bi₃SbO₇: 2.27 eV
- Bi₂O₃: 2.34 eV

BiSbO₄, around Sb 0.5, is predicted at 3.06 eV, too wide to absorb this light. I didn't measure anything with more than 25% Sb.

The model predictions didn't hold up: the phase with the lowest predicted gap (index 5) did worse than Bi₂O₃. So these three points don't show a clear trend. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so I never checked which phases actually formed at each point. Most of the Bi-rich range is still unmeasured, so a better composition could be sitting between the points I tested.
